clocks.label: KYIV PAUSE ENDS
clocks.why: Putin's 72-hour instruction that no strikes hit the Ukrainian capital, reciprocated by Zelenskyy, runs out. This is the dated falsifier on GEO-005, held at 20 per cent today: if it lapses with no extension and no jointly acknowledged text, the number goes back to 17 and yesterday's raise is scored a miss rather than deferred. Note what the pause does not cover - 108 Russian and 258 Ukrainian drones flew overnight outside the two capitals.

clocks.label: VENEZUELA TEXT
clocks.why: The signing session Caracas scheduled. This prices GEO-022 at 36 per cent: if it passes with no published instrument - no governing law, no arbitration seat, no named sanctions authorisation - a 100-year concession exists only as a briefing. The premeditation tell is not equity, it is an awarded dredging contract or a heavy-crude terminal tender.

clocks.label: FOMC DECISION
clocks.why: The meeting behind GEO-029, opened today at 70 per cent. July held at 3.50-3.75 with THREE members dissenting FOR a hike; PCE runs 3.7 per cent year-on-year and 4.1 annualised over six months. This is the clock that decides whether the world's reserve central bank tightens INTO an oil supply shock - the 1973-74 error in either direction - with the ten-year already through our 4.75 red line.

clocks.label: BOJ DECISION
clocks.why: Two days after the Fed, and the clock behind GEO-025, cut to 26 per cent today. Japan is where the world borrows cheaply. The carry unwind needs BOTH legs - a Tokyo surprise and a dovish repricing of the Fed - and a hawkish Fed removes the second, which is why this was cut rather than raised on a week of rate news.

clocks.label: HORMUZ FALSIFIER
clocks.why: Our own dated falsifier, published in advance so it can be scored against us, and deliberately NOT reinterpreted again today. It requires an attack on a laden tanker inside the INTERNATIONAL LANES. If none occurs by this date AND Muscat publishes a minesweeping calendar, the recurrence read is a MISS: GEO-001 back toward 21, GEO-003 back to about 38.

clocks.label: XI SUMMIT
clocks.why: The state visit GEO-006 rides at 89 per cent and GEO-012 at 31, and the date Washington wants its 7.5 per cent overcapacity finding published before. Brent's band question resolves the same day on a DAILY CLOSE - our first Brier score, and the reason the intraday $99.38 of 2 September did not count.

speculation.obs: A satellite-analysis team has watched two months of construction go up at China's most secretive flight-test base, and the hangars are the wrong size for fighters. As published by Misbar's team at Al-Araby TV, a comparison of European Sentinel-2 imagery from 2 July and 1 September 2026 shows a marked acceleration at Lop Nur air base in Xinjiang: a new concrete taxiway running parallel to the roughly five-kilometre main runway now nearly complete, a newly connected 130-metre circular apron at the northern end, and four large structures under construction on the western side, each around 80 metres wide.
speculation.src: Misbar / Al-Araby TV analysis team, published 3 September 2026, using European Space Agency Sentinel-2 imagery dated 2 July and 1 September 2026
speculation.read: Labelled inference. The load-bearing observation is the hangar width, not the runway - 80 metres is built for large wingspans, not for fighters, and the analysts read it as capacity for something in the strategic-bomber or large-airframe class. Lop Nur is already the venue where imagery caught what are described as sixth-generation prototypes, the J-36 and J-XDS, in the previous year. The reason this belongs on a geopolitical board rather than an aviation one is timing: infrastructure is the slowest and most honest signal a state emits, because you cannot fake a taxiway, and this one is being poured on a schedule that fits a stated 2030 deployment ambition. Sentinel-2 is free and public, so the claim is checkable by anyone with the coordinates - which is why the grade is credible rather than corroborated, pending a second imagery house.
speculation.falsifier: A second independent imagery analysis - Planet, Maxar, or a defence-research institute - describing the same structures at the same dimensions upgrades this to corroborated. Hangars completing at a width consistent with fighters, or the structures turning out to be maintenance or storage sheds, kills the large-airframe read outright.

speculation.obs: The permit regime Tehran now describes in its own statements was visible in AIS tracks months before any state admitted to one. As reported by gCaptain from analysis by Martin Kelly, head of advisory at EOS Risk Group, a set of outbound vessels diverted from the standard southern lane toward Iranian-controlled waters before being allowed to continue - a pattern Kelly read as ships being verified before exit rather than seized.
speculation.src: gCaptain, reporting AIS-track analysis by Martin Kelly of EOS Risk Group; corroborated in kind by Windward's published dark-activity counts around Iranian anchorage zones
speculation.read: Labelled inference, and it stays on the board because it is the entry the headlines keep catching up with. A tracker looking at a handful of hulls called a licensing system before any government used the word, and the IRGC has since used 'restricted' and 'unauthorised' in its own statements about the strait. This is the species we hunt: a physical pattern observed by a specialist, with no official story attached, that later acquires one.
speculation.falsifier: A run of outbound transits on the standard southern lane, unqueried and at pre-crisis volume, kills the permit read outright - the whole claim is that ships are being routed to check in. A published account by an owner or master describing a clearance request would confirm it.

speculation.obs: The trackers can put a zero on the blockade. As reported by MarineLink from Kpler, Vortexa and TankerTrackers.com data, no Iranian crude cargo successfully transited the Strait of Hormuz to China for seven straight weeks after the blockade was reinstated on 14 July, with August loadings of roughly 220,000 to 255,000 barrels a day against about 740,000 in July and some 2 million in March. Samir Madani of TankerTrackers counted 29 tankers inside the strait holding 36.11 million barrels, and the same reporting puts 27 sanctioned Iran-linked tankers waiting off Sri Lanka in ballast - empty.
speculation.src: MarineLink, 1 September 2026, reporting Kpler, Vortexa and TankerTrackers.com counts, with Homayoun Falakshahi of Kpler and Samir Madani of TankerTrackers named on the record
speculation.read: Labelled inference. Empty is worse for Tehran than loaded-and-waiting: not cargo queued for sale but capacity that cannot get home to load. It also explains the sequence rather than merely accompanying it - a state with no exportable barrels has no economic instrument left, so it reaches for a geographic one and starts charging for other people's passage. Falakshahi's point is the one to carry: an export collapse of this size drains foreign-currency income and pushes a government toward printing, which is the mechanism by which a naval blockade becomes an inflation number.
speculation.falsifier: A confirmed Iranian crude discharge in China, or loadings recovering back through 500,000 barrels a day, means the blockade is leaking and the pressure read is wrong. The ballast fleet off Sri Lanka reversing course toward Iranian terminals would be the early tell.

dossiers.name: Iran

glance.government: Islamic Republic - a clerical-military hybrid in which the security institutions have been ascendant since the February-May war
glance.leader: Mojtaba Khamenei, Supreme Leader since 8 Mar 2026, not verifiably seen in public for roughly six months; Masoud Pezeshkian president; IRGC commander-in-chief Ahmad Vahidi the operative center
glance.gdp: Roughly $300-390bn nominal depending on source; forecast to contract about 5% in 2026 with inflation near 70% and the rial at a record 2.02m to the dollar
glance.military: About 570,000-610,000 active (IISS puts it near 570,000) plus roughly 350,000 reserves; the IRGC Navy, not the regular navy, holds the strait
glance.influence: Transit rights and mine inventory at Hormuz, anti-ship missiles, Iraqi and Yemeni networks - set against oil revenue the central bank governor himself describes as having fallen to zero

dossiers.summary: Start with the constraint, not the man. Iran is a state whose one convertible asset - the barrel - has stopped moving, which is why its remaining leverage is geographic rather than economic, and why it is spent in advertised doses rather than banked. The desk that decides is the IRGC Navy and the new wartime security committee, not the presidency and not the invisible Leader: Washington routed its own peace offer through career Guard commanders, and Iran's president has said on state television that communicating with Khamenei is very difficult. That produces exactly the behaviour this board keeps recording - a volley at forewarned bases in Jordan that was almost entirely intercepted, mines laid and lanes conditionally cleared, six near-breakthroughs that each end in a restated condition. Prospect theory says a cornered regime gambles, but a regime whose survival runs through an institution that profits from the crisis has an interest in holding the temperature where it can still choose it. The falsifier is a strike that actually kills Americans, or a verified minesweeping calendar with published coordinates - either would show the temperature is no longer being chosen.

concerns: Mine and anti-ship capability at Hormuz is intact and reversible - a cleared lane is a maintenance schedule, not a settlement
Succession is unresolved in practice: an unseen Leader plus an IRGC that answers Washington's messages is a leadership fiction with a real chain of command underneath
Oil revenue near zero against 70% inflation removes the economic off-ramp that would normally price restraint
Escalation is now probabilistic rather than intentional - interception rates, not decisions, separate a message from a casualty event

Retaliation has gone HORIZONTAL: fire into US facilities in Jordan, Bahrain and Kuwait in a single night widens the number of surfaces on which the interception equilibrium can fail, and converts Gulf hosts from venues into potential parties

The war has reached the LOADING POINT: Iranian state media says four US missiles hit a tanker six miles off Kharg on 5 September, and Iran fired anti-ship and ballistic missiles toward the strait the day before. Unconfirmed, and the terminals themselves are still unstruck - but the one asset with any convertible value left is now inside the target set

dossiers.name: Russia

glance.government: Presidential autocracy with a managed legislature; State Duma elections due September 2026
glance.leader: Vladimir Putin - the only decider on the war file; Peskov is a thermostat, not an actor
glance.population: About 144 million (2026 estimate; occupied-territory counting disputed)
glance.gdp: Roughly $2.7tn nominal; the government cut its 2026 growth forecast toward 0.4-1%, with oil and gas revenue reported down more than 25%
glance.military: About 1.3 million active with roughly 2 million reserves; defence spending near 6.3-6.5% of GDP
glance.influence: Sanctioned-barrel logistics including the Arctic route, Africa Corps guarantees in the Sahel, energy leverage over Europe, veto and nuclear status

dossiers.summary: Moscow's constraint is refining and money, not morale. Ukrainian deep strikes have pushed refinery runs to about 3.6m barrels a day, the lowest since 2002, and the fuel export ban first imposed in July is being weighed for a second extension - each extension a public admission of how much capacity is offline. The deciding desks are the defence and finance ministries rather than the foreign ministry: the September Duma election and the 6.3-6.5% of GDP the war costs are what price the negotiating posture, which is why the deep pause Peskov announced reads as a bargaining position taken from a front that is still moving at Pokrovsk. Watch where the state chose to spend a scarce asset this weekend - Africa Corps, roughly 200-300 personnel supplied overland through Burkina Faso, was used to save a junta in Niamey, buying an advertisement and incurring an obligation in the same act. The observables that would move this file are not statements but airlift and diesel: Flight Unit 224 traffic above its six-flight run rate, or refinery runs recovering past 4m barrels a day.

concerns: The fuel and refining constraint is the real bind - denial is working where punishment has not, and Kyiv is aiming at exactly that
The announced campaign against Ukraine's grid is punishment by Pape's definition, with a poor historical conversion into concessions
Sahel guarantees now carry a defend-the-palace obligation a 200-300 person detachment cannot scale
September Duma elections and a possible post-election reserve call-up are the domestic clock every diplomatic signal is priced against

The covert front against the supplier coalition is now formally attributed: Berlin blames Moscow for an explosive drone at Leipzig/Halle and closes the Bonn consulate on Sept 18, with the EU calling it state-sponsored terrorism - salami tactics against logistics rather than against forces

First reciprocated pause of the war, and it is a bargaining instrument rather than fatigue: Putin ordered no strikes on Kyiv for 72 hours from midnight on 5 September, explicitly tied to the American envoys' visit, hours after striking Ukrainian airports and infrastructure and with Ryabkov restating that Washington must accept realities on the ground

dossiers.name: Ukraine

glance.government: Wartime presidential republic under martial law; national elections suspended for the duration
glance.leader: Volodymyr Zelenskyy, constrained by coalition dependence; Rustem Umerov holds both the negotiating brief and the intelligence file
glance.population: About 39.5 million on mid-2026 estimates - wartime displacement makes every figure soft
glance.gdp: Roughly $225bn nominal (2025); the EU agreed a package of about EUR 90bn for 2026-27, funded by market borrowing rather than by seizing the roughly EUR 210bn of frozen Russian assets
glance.military: About 677,000 active on the IISS count; larger figures circulate and are not verified
glance.influence: A deep-strike drone campaign that has taken Russian refining to a 24-year low, the Black Sea corridor, and the political weight of being the coalition's test case

dossiers.summary: Kyiv's constraint is arithmetic - manpower, interceptors and a donor calendar - and it sets the strategy rather than following from it. The one instrument Ukraine owns outright is the drone campaign against Russian refineries, which is denial in Pape's sense and is measurably working; nearly everything else is rented from capitals that vote. That dependence is why the deciding desk is now split between the general staff and a negotiating channel run through Washington, and why Zelenskyy has to say yes to the joint Western plan and no to surrender in the same breath. It also explains Myla: an army under sustained deep strike disperses munitions into settlements, which lowers the odds of losing a depot and raises the odds of a night like Friday's, when 38 people died mostly from what the warehouse contained. The falsifiable claim for the winter is that Russia's fuel constraint shapes Russian behaviour more than blackouts shape Ukrainian negotiating positions - if Kyiv's position visibly softens under grid attack while Moscow's does not under fuel shortage, the model is wrong and we say so.

concerns: The announced Russian campaign against the electricity grid arrives with winter and with air-defence stocks already rationed
Pokrovsk is the axis Moscow names when it explains why it is in no hurry to talk; its fall would be a step change, not a line move
Funding is market-borrowed rather than asset-backed, which puts the money on a European political calendar
Dispersal of munitions into inhabited areas makes mass-casualty events recurrent regardless of anyone's aimpoint

dossiers.name: China

glance.government: Party-state under the most centralized leadership since Mao; a recent command purge reshaped the military timetable
glance.leader: Xi Jinping; Wang Yi carries the foreign file with delegated authority
glance.gdp: About $20.9tn nominal (IMF, 2026); 4.7% growth in the first half against a 4.5-5% target, July exports up 23.9% year on year
glance.military: About 2.0 million active, the largest standing force in the world; announced defence budget in the $280bn range
glance.influence: Buyer of last resort for sanctioned barrels, rare earths and the export machine, coast-guard jurisdiction pressure around Taiwan and the East China Sea, and a summit Washington wants

dossiers.summary: Beijing's constraint this quarter is the calendar, not the doctrine. A state visit on 24 September and a tariff truce expiring in November are both worth more than any concession on Iranian crude, which is why the buying continues while the rhetoric stays defiant - and why Treasury sanctioned an Egyptian bank's UAE branches rather than a Chinese one. An enforcer that keeps picking the cheapest nail is telling you which nail is expensive. The desk to watch is not the foreign ministry but the coast guard and the customs administration: PLA sorties around Taiwan have been declining while jurisdictional assertion has been rising, and that ratchet - salami tactics in Schelling's sense, slices too thin to fight over individually - is the actual instrument. Read the summit as accumulation under cover of detente rather than as a thaw, and keep the discount small: announced head-of-state visits with active staff preparation happen about 90% of the time. The tell that breaks the benign read is a coast-guard action inside the visit window; the tell that breaks the leverage read is a blocking designation on a top-ten Chinese bank before 24 September.

concerns: Coast-guard normalization and seabed mapping are precondition-building around Taiwan, not the event itself
China is the load-bearing leak in the Iran sanctions siege - Mulder's rule is that a siege is only as tight as its leakage path
The tariff truce expires in November, just after the summit, which is where a cheap concession becomes an expensive one
A defiant public line paired with quiet compliance makes intent unreadable from statements; only flows settle it

dossiers.name: Israel

glance.government: Parliamentary democracy; the Knesset dissolved in July and the election is set for 27 October 2026
glance.leader: Benjamin Netanyahu, prime minister; Israel Katz defence minister and the cabinet's designated hawk
glance.gdp: About $720bn nominal on 2026 estimates, with defence spending near 8% of GDP
glance.influence: Air superiority over the Levant, the Washington relationship, and an undeclared nuclear status the state has never confirmed

dossiers.summary: Read every Israeli decision for the next seven weeks through 27 October. That is the constraint, and it is a calendar rather than a character: a prime minister facing an election needs deliverables that are visible, mapped and finished, which is exactly what a declared security zone is. On 4 September Katz said the capture of the Ali al-Taher ridge completes the phase of securing control in southern Lebanon and that there will be no withdrawal until Hezbollah is disarmed throughout the country - a condition the Lebanese state has never been able to meet, which makes the presence open-ended by construction. The desk that decides is not the cabinet podium but Northern Command's force-generation math and the finance ministry's reserve-duty bill, because holding ground costs manpower in a way air power does not. Note also the direction this cuts: history says a held buffer produces chronic attrition rather than episodic campaigns, which is why this board CUT its multi-week-campaign odds on the day the zone was declared. Separately, national security minister Ben Gvir published a twenty-page plan for what he calls voluntary emigration of Gaza's population - 250,000 in the first year and the remainder over six more. It is a minister's document rather than cabinet policy, and forced transfer of civilians from occupied territory is a war crime under the Geneva Conventions; it is logged here as a coalition signal, not as a programme.

concerns: The 27 October election makes restraint politically expensive at exactly the wrong moment
A withdrawal condition the Lebanese state cannot satisfy converts an operation into an occupation by definition
The Lebanon framework still has no third-party verifier and the party being disarmed rejects the premise
Ministerial transfer plans for Gaza, even unimplemented, carry legal and coalition exposure that outlasts the cabinet

dossiers.name: Germany

glance.government: Federal parliamentary republic; coalition government under a chancellor with weak approval numbers
glance.leader: Friedrich Merz, chancellor; Alexander Dobrindt at the Interior Ministry carries the attribution and the police file, which is why the response is expulsions rather than an alliance consultation
glance.gdp: Roughly $4.9tn nominal - unverified against a current print; the binding number this quarter is energy input cost rather than headline output
glance.military: About 182,000 active on standard counts, with a rearmament programme running against recruitment shortfalls; unverified against a current IISS figure
glance.influence: Europe's largest industrial gas consumer, the logistics bridge to Ukraine through Leipzig/Halle, and the swing vote on every EU sanctions and energy instrument

dossiers.summary: Germany's constraint is a vice with an energy jaw and a security jaw, and both tightened this week. It replaced Russian pipeline gas with seaborne LNG, which traded a political dependency for a maritime one - so a war at Hormuz now reaches German industry directly, with continental storage near 62 percent against a seasonal norm around 79. At the same time it is the physical bridge over which munitions reach Ukraine, which is precisely why an explosive drone came down at Leipzig/Halle rather than at a barracks. Read the response for what it reveals about the ceiling: the desk that acted was the Interior Ministry, and the instruments were a consulate closure, a cultural-institute contract and visa tightening - the diplomatic rail, chosen because it is cheap, reversible and does not require asking twenty-six other governments for permission. The official story is resolve; the incentive read is a chancellor with poor ratings who gains from a clear adversary, which is a reason to scrutinise the timing rather than to assume it.

concerns: Gas storage near 62 percent with winter arriving is an industrial-cost problem before it is a household one, and German industry is the marginal European buyer

A sabotage campaign aimed at logistics rather than forces sits deliberately below any alliance threshold - which is what makes it repeatable, and Lavrov has now answered the attribution by calling it the start of a real war
The attribution was published without forensics or charges, so its political durability depends on evidence Berlin has not yet shown
Moscow has promised to mirror the expulsions, which costs Germany intelligence access it may value more than the consulate it closed
Saxony-Anhalt votes today with the AfD near 40 per cent: the constraint on Berlin's Russia and energy policy is about to include a Land government it may not be able to exclude

dossiers.name: United States

glance.government: Federal presidential republic; midterm elections 3 November 2026
glance.leader: Donald Trump; Scott Bessent at Treasury, Marco Rubio at State, Pete Hegseth at Defense, Kevin Warsh at the Federal Reserve
glance.gdp: Roughly $30tn nominal on standard 2026 estimates - unverified against a current print; federal debt past $40tn
glance.military: About 1.34 million active with roughly 770,000 reserve and National Guard; budget in the $900bn range
glance.influence: Dollar clearing and OFAC designations, CENTCOM escort of the strait, and a rate path that prices everyone else's oil bill

dossiers.summary: The American constraint hardened today and it is arithmetic rather than politics. August payrolls came in at 162,000 against a 53,000 consensus with unemployment at 4.1%, which removes the soft-landing argument for cutting; simultaneously diesel set an all-time record at $5.820 a gallon on a refining shortage no interest rate can fix. That is the RESCUE WITHHELD configuration - a market pricing help in a shock where help does not exist - and the long end already agrees, with the ten-year at 4.79% and the thirty-year at 5.27%, both above this board's published red lines, and the reverse-repo buffer down to $0.70bn. The desk that decides is not the podium: it is the FOMC, the refiners' turnaround calendar and the weekly EIA distillate print, in that order of who can actually change the number. Foreign policy is being run on the same logic - allies invoiced for contributions at Hormuz, a Venezuelan venture organised around one man's legal exposure rather than around built infrastructure, and a president who declined this week to say whether the United States would defend Britain in another Falklands war. Each of those is leverage bought cheaply now against a commitment payable later.

concerns: Record diesel is the invisible half of the inflation problem, because it prices freight, farming and heating rather than only the pump
A hot labour print into a hiking debate removes the monetary rescue markets keep assuming
Enforcement at Hormuz is now a standing commitment - a lane you must keep clearing is not a victory
Alliance ambiguity is being used as leverage in three theatres at once, and credibility spent in one is not recoverable in another
Confirmed American casualties would collapse the intercepted-volley equilibrium the whole restraint posture rests on

dossiers.name: Japan

glance.government: Constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary system; Bank of Japan policy decision due 18 September 2026
glance.leader: Emperor Naruhito as head of state; the Bank of Japan governorship is the office that matters for this file - the policy board, not the cabinet, sets the variable the world is watching
glance.gdp: Roughly $4.2tn nominal on standard 2026 estimates - unverified against a current print; policy rate 0.75 per cent, a thirty-year high, with ten-year government bond yields near 3 per cent for the first time since 1996
glance.military: Self-Defense Forces of about 247,000 active personnel; defence spending on a path toward 2 per cent of GDP
glance.influence: The world's cheap funding currency, one of the largest foreign holders of US Treasuries, and a carry trade estimated anywhere between $500bn and over $4tn depending on definition

dossiers.summary: Japan appears on this board for a plumbing reason rather than a diplomatic one, and it is the reason the board opened a new forecast today. For thirty years Japan supplied the world with money that cost nothing - zero rates from 1999, then quantitative and qualitative easing from 2013 - and the world spent it on everything from Mexican bonds to American technology. That arrangement is now unwinding, not because Tokyo chose a new geopolitics but because Japan finally has inflation, imported partly through a weak yen and partly through an energy bill that this year's Hormuz disruption has made worse. The constraint on the policy board is therefore domestic and blunt: households are angry about food and fuel prices, exporters and the equity index need the weak currency, and every previous attempt to tighten has met that second constituency and delivered less than markets priced. The desk that decides is the BoJ policy board on 18 September; the desk that transmits is the leveraged fund complex and the Japanese insurers and pension funds holding vast foreign bond portfolios. Watch the yen rather than the statement - a hike with the currency through 150 is the confirmation leg, and a hike with the yen drifting back above 160 is another false start in a long series.

concerns: A disorderly carry unwind transmits a Tokyo rate decision into global asset prices within hours, as it did in August 2024
The size of the borrowed-yen stack is genuinely unknown - published estimates span an order of magnitude
Higher domestic yields give Japanese institutions a reason to repatriate from Treasuries exactly as US issuance runs heaviest
Imported energy costs are the transmission line from the Strait of Hormuz into Japanese inflation and therefore into this policy decision

scenarios.q: What if the Gulf exchange stops being target-matched?
scenarios.read: For six months this has been an equilibrium held by arithmetic rather than by restraint: target-matched volleys, high interception rates, and two governments that each get to claim a result at home. This weekend it widened twice in a day. The US moved from military assets to COMMERCIAL HULLS, confirming strikes on three Iranian tankers; Iran moved from shipping to an American platform, claiming a hit on an unmanned US vessel. Both sides picked targets that cannot bleed - a tanker crew evacuates, a drone ship has nobody aboard - which is what tells you the equilibrium is being stretched deliberately rather than broken accidentally.

stages.s: Within 14 days: a second, separately dated strike on shipping inside the northern Gulf loading zone, or a confirmed hit on a laden tanker with no Iranian link inside the international lanes. Falsifier: a fortnight of quiet, or Muscat publishing corridor coordinates.

Within 30 days: a confirmed American death or a struck US-flagged hull - the published CRITICAL trigger on this board, still unfired after two missile attacks on warships. Falsifier: unfired on 6 October, logged as scored rather than deferred.

Within 60 days of such an event: a sustained multi-week campaign against Iranian STATE targets, which is GEO-003 at 49 per cent. Note the gap: tankers and launchers are not state targets and do not resolve it.
Beyond: a strike on Kharg's loading terminals themselves, ending Iranian seaborne export rather than taxing it. Most branches die at stage A, which is why the terminals are wired separately.

scenarios.falsifier: Fourteen days with no further attack on shipping plus a published minesweeping calendar out of Muscat kills this branch, sends GEO-003 back toward 38 and GEO-001 back toward 21 - scored as a miss, not deferred.

scenarios.q: What if the Fed hikes into an oil supply shock?
scenarios.read: This is the branch nobody is watching and it sits under every other story on the board. The mechanism is a category error with a long pedigree: an oil-driven price rise is a SUPPLY event, and a policy rate is a DEMAND instrument, so tightening against it treats the symptom in the only place the tool reaches. Blinder and Bernanke's work on supply shocks is the standing argument for looking through it; three FOMC members dissented for a hike anyway in July, PCE runs 3.7 per cent, and Brent is under $96 because OPEC+ just declined to add barrels. The second-order question is the one that matters for everything else: a hawkish Fed widens the dollar-yen differential, which suppresses the carry unwind, and raises the cost of every 2021-22 vintage refinancing now coming due.

stages.s: Within 10 days: a 25bp increase on 16 September. Falsifier: a hold with the dissent bloc shrinking, which sends GEO-029 from 70 to 45 and is scored, not deferred.

Within 90 days: the ten-year holds above 4.75 and the thirty-year above 5.25 for a full month - the red-board lines - with the Fed's bill programme still running. Falsifier: the long end falling back through both lines, which would say the market read the hike as credibility rather than as fiscal strain.

Within 6 months: a funding event rather than a price move - a failed or heavily tailed thirty-year auction, or a visible strain in dealer balance sheets. Falsifier: six months of clean auctions, which scores the strain read a miss.
Beyond: the standing bill programme is expanded or renamed rather than sunset, which is GEO-019 at 93 per cent. Most branches die at stage A or B and this one is written to.

scenarios.falsifier: A hold on 16 September AND 4-5 November with fewer dissents each time kills this branch and scores the tightening read a miss.

scenarios.q: What if Germany's firewall holds and the state becomes ungovernable?
scenarios.read: The result lands tonight, so this is the last time this branch can be written honestly rather than retrospectively. The mechanism is arithmetic, not sentiment: a cordon sanitaire denies partners and does nothing to a party that reaches a majority alone, while costing the excluding bloc its own options. The CDU in Saxony-Anhalt has ruled out both the AfD and Die Linke and polls around 22.5 per cent against the AfD's 40-41.7. So the interesting failure mode is not a far-right government - it is no government at all, and a second election fought on the question of who made the state ungovernable.

stages.s: Tonight: the AfD takes the most seats but falls short of an absolute majority. Falsifier: an outright seat majority, which resolves GEO-028 quickly and kills this branch by the other door. Watch the FDP and BSW lines under five per cent - wasted ballots redistribute upward and decide it.

Within 90 days: a CDU-led minority government, or a CDU arrangement with Die Linke that breaks a second taboo in order to preserve the first. Falsifier: a stable conventional coalition seated without either.

Within 18 months: repeat elections in the Land, or an AfD Minister-President anywhere in Germany - GEO-028, held at 16 per cent today rather than pre-judged. Falsifier: a government seated and surviving a budget vote.
Beyond: the federal CDU formally softens the Brandmauer at Land level. Most branches die at stage A or B and this one is designed to.

scenarios.falsifier: A conventional coalition seated in Magdeburg within 90 days kills this branch outright and scores the ungovernability read a miss.

scenarios.q: What if the export-control regime is already leaking faster than it is tightened?
scenarios.read: The mechanism is that an Entity List is a list of NAMES, and a name is the cheapest thing a company owns. Reporting today traces a blacklisted Chinese server maker continuing to obtain top-end American AI processors through a renamed, US-domiciled affiliate and third-party resellers that were never themselves listed. Farrell and Newman's weaponized-interdependence framework predicts exactly this decay curve: a chokepoint works while the target must pass through a node you control, and erodes as the target restructures around the node. The policy question is whether Washington answers with ownership tests and end-use verification - expensive, slow, and it annoys allies - or with more names, which is cheap and loses.

stages.s: Within 60 days: a Commerce or BIS action adding affiliates, or a formal ownership-threshold rule closing the subsidiary gap. Falsifier: sixty days with no rulemaking and no new listings, which would say the leak is tolerated.

Within 6 months: enforcement moves from listing to LIABILITY - a penalty, settlement or indictment against a US seller or reseller rather than a foreign buyer. Falsifier: no US-side enforcement action.

Within 12 months: allied jurisdictions adopt a matching ownership test, which is what turns a US control into a coalition standard - Mulder's condition for a sanction that actually binds. Falsifier: allies decline and the control stays unilateral.
Beyond: the control is abandoned in substance and traded away as summit currency. Most branches die at stage A.

scenarios.falsifier: A published ownership-threshold rule plus a US-side enforcement action within six months kills the decay read and scores it a miss.

chatter.claim: That the German result will be voided by procedure rather than by votes - every other party assembled into a coalition purely to keep a 44.5 per cent plurality out of office, offered as proof that the elections there are advisory. The companion claim is that half of today's AfD voters did not vote in the last election at all, and that the CDU alone lost over eighty thousand of its previous voters to them.
chatter.spread: The second German election thread at nearly 380 replies, the busiest thing on /pol/ tonight, plus a dedicated vote-migration thread.
chatter.read: The rigged-by-procedure frame, and its kernel is unusually strong - coalitions that exclude the largest party are a real and openly stated feature of German practice, so the claim describes something true and then relabels it theft. The vote-migration numbers are the genuinely checkable part: district-level returns are among the most auditable data in Europe and will confirm or destroy the mobilisation claim within days. Record 80 per cent turnout against 60.3 in 2021 is already consistent with it.

chatter.claim: An ethnic-scapegoat narrative is circulating around the AfD itself, in which the party is said to be secretly infiltrated and controlled by Jews and its wins therefore hollow.
chatter.spread: A thread on /pol/ at around fifty replies, running through the election coverage.
chatter.read: The technique to name is the unfalsifiable-purity move: it pre-explains any future disappointment - a coalition, a moderation, a policy retreat - as hidden infiltration rather than as ordinary party behaviour, which makes the belief permanently safe from evidence. It surfaces most reliably at the exact moment a movement wins big and then discovers it still cannot govern, which is tonight.

chatter.claim: That Iran has begun sinking American supercarriers, and that the size of the US answer proves the two warships were hurt far worse than admitted - you do not destroy three tankers over missiles that missed.
chatter.spread: A dedicated thread at nearly 300 replies alongside the Persia-Israel general, the busiest recurring thread on the board.
chatter.read: The damage-is-being-concealed frame with the brakes off - no hull name, no imagery, no insurer entry, only escalation of the previous post. The inference runs backwards: retaliation is scaled to a pre-approved target set, not to injury received. The kernel we will not pretend away is that CENTCOM remains the sole account of what happened to those two ships.

chatter.claim: That the Amazon cargo 767 that overran the runway at Miami International killed multiple people and that the toll is being managed downward - and, in the same threads, that a freight aircraft crossing a public road is the visible end of an airframe and maintenance decline nobody will name.
chatter.spread: Two happening threads opened within minutes of each other, one at over eighty replies, built around a single X video post.
chatter.read: The standard casualty-suppression frame, which attaches to every aviation event in the first two hours because that is the window in which official counts genuinely are incomplete - the belief is manufactured by the lag, not by a cover-up. The second half is the more interesting one and it is partly checkable: runway excursions are a real and tracked category, and the NTSB docket on this airframe will exist. Worth logging now so the eventual official count can be scored against tonight's claim.

chatter.claim: That the Indonesian eruptions are the start of a volcanic winter and a global food collapse - Krakatoa framed as finally awake, with a companion thread claiming five to seven simultaneous eruptions since 31 August and a food-scarcity argument that people should be planting nut trees and raising livestock now.
chatter.spread: A breaking thread at over 200 replies, a second seven-volcanoes thread, a food-scarcity thread at nearly 150, and the /biz/ stock market general running all day under a Volcanic Winter edition title.
chatter.read: The civilisational-collapse frame attaching to a real event within hours, now fused to a trade. The checkable kernel is genuine and small: Indonesian volcanoes are erupting, ash has disrupted hundreds of flights, and that is a serious and routine hazard there. The leap is scale - a volcanic winter needs a stratospheric sulphur injection orders of magnitude larger, and 1883 is borrowed as a template because it is the only Krakatoa most people know.

chatter.claim: That the shutdown of USAID has revealed how much of global civil society it was quietly paying for - NGOs closing worldwide, media outlets folding, cultural scenes collapsing, all offered as retrospective proof that the whole apparatus was one funded operation rather than an ecosystem.
chatter.spread: A /pol/ thread at over 230 replies presenting the list as a greentext of consequences, with the same list recirculating on X.
chatter.read: The everything-was-funded frame, and it has the strongest documentary kernel of anything on the board this week: USAID grant records are public, the agency did fund media development, health programmes and civil-society organisations across dozens of countries, and closures downstream of a funding withdrawal are real and expected. The overreach is inferring purpose from dependence - an organisation that took a grant is not thereby an instrument, and the list conflates a health programme in Malawi with a magazine somebody dislikes.

chatter.claim: That American strategists are openly proposing military strikes on Chinese data centres to stop China developing artificial general intelligence, and that this is now a live option rather than a thought experiment.
chatter.spread: A /pol/ thread at around ninety replies quoting the proposal directly, recirculating from policy-paper commentary on X.
chatter.read: This one is downstream of something real and is being reported as if it were policy. Published strategy writing has genuinely floated preventive action against adversary AI infrastructure as a scenario - the well-known example argues states may treat a rival's decisive AI lead the way they treat a nuclear breakout. The distance being collapsed is between a think-tank scenario and a target list, which is the same move that turns every wargame into a leak. Worth watching because if datacentre capacity ever does get named in an export-control or force-posture document, this narrative will already have a year of head start.

chatter.claim: That the masked blockade of the Port of Dover was deliberately tolerated by British police - either to manufacture a later crackdown or because the state has decided not to contest the street - with a council leader's own complaint that police were slow to respond offered as the evidence.
chatter.spread: The British politics general and a successor thread, together at around 175 replies, both leading with the same BBC link.
chatter.read: The deliberate-tolerance frame, and the kernel here is a genuine on-the-record grievance rather than an invention: a named council figure did publicly criticise the response time, which is why this narrative travels further than most. The gap is between slow and permitted - resourcing failures and political decisions produce identical footage, and the boring explanation predicts it just as well. What would settle it is the operational log or an inspectorate review, and neither is likely to be published quickly.

chatter.claim: That Erika Kirk is an intelligence asset - a thread assembling a 2012 pageant record, an appearance in an early video, unexplained travel to Romania and a claimed Epstein adjacency into the argument that she was placed in Charlie Kirk's orbit by an agency before they met.
chatter.spread: A /pol/ thread at over 250 replies, running alongside several other Charlie Kirk threads on the board today.
chatter.read: The intel-asset frame, the domestic-politics cousin of the honeypot story, and the most common way a movement metabolises the loss of a figure it cannot otherwise explain. The technique to name is biographical accumulation: a pageant, a video credit and a flight are each individually mundane, and the argument works entirely by stacking them until the pile feels like a pattern. There is no documentary claim in it - no filing, no contract, no named handler - which is what separates it from the genuinely documented history of media-agency relationships people reach for as precedent.

chatter.claim: That the Bank for International Settlements has quietly picked the winners of tokenised settlement - a new BIS paper on putting official government statistics such as GDP and inflation on a blockchain is being read on the markets board as an institutional endorsement of specific ledgers.
chatter.spread: A /biz/ thread at around seventy-five replies, cross-posting into the coin generals.
chatter.read: The endorsement-by-mention frame, and it is the single most reliable misreading of central-bank research there is - a BIS working paper describing a technique is routinely traded as a BIS decision. The kernel is real and worth watching on its own terms: cryptographically committing official statistics is a genuine proposal with real implications for how sanctions data, reserve reporting and settlement finality get audited. The leap is from a paper naming an architecture to an institution naming an asset.

chatter.claim: Two markets narratives running together: that the yen has rugged and the carry trade is unwinding now, and that the US president is threatening to embargo countries running trade deficits with America unless the Federal Reserve cuts rates - the second offered as proof that trade policy is being used as a lever on monetary policy.
chatter.spread: Two /biz/ threads at around fifty-five replies each, inside the day's stock market general.
chatter.read: The tariffs-as-monetary-coercion frame, and it maps onto a real structural question this desk already carries: the Fed decides on 16 September and the Bank of Japan on 18 September, and a carry unwind needs both legs, not one. The kernel is that pressure on the Fed from the executive branch is documented and continuing. The leap is treating a threat as a mechanism - an embargo does not set the policy rate, and the board is reading intent as transmission.

chatter.claim: That today's disasters were signposted in advance - the paranormal board's long-running predictive-programming thread, now on its second edition with the image limit reached, is collecting film and television frames read as advance notice of the volcano, the aircraft crash and the Gulf exchange.
chatter.spread: A thread at nearly 290 replies on /x/, alongside a memory-holed thread at around 185 recirculating older claims.
chatter.read: The predictive-programming frame, which is the purest example of a belief system that cannot be falsified by design - with enough frames of fiction, any event has a precedent, and the search is conducted after the fact. It is worth monitoring not for content but as a volatility gauge: the thread's size tracks how unsettled the wider board feels, and it grew today alongside a volcano, an airliner and a shooting war. Belief is the data here, not the claim.

easy.bottomLine: Today had a lot of noise and one quiet fact. The noise: Iran said it blew up an American robot boat near the entrance to the Gulf, and the American military said that is simply not true - and nobody has shown a damaged boat. The quiet fact: the big oil-producing countries met and decided NOT to pump any more oil, even though oil is expensive right now. Countries usually love selling more when prices are high. Choosing not to usually means they cannot, or they are saving it. Elsewhere, a far-right party won an election in one German state by a huge margin, and American envoys visited Ukraine and left without a deal.
easy.risk: Still HIGH, and we did not move it. We wrote down in advance what would take us to the top level: an American killed, or an American ship actually hit and confirmed. Neither has happened. Iran's claim about the robot boat does not count, because a claim is not proof and the two sides are the only ones telling the story. If someone photographs a damaged boat, that changes.
easy.markets: Oil is near 96 dollars a barrel, the most expensive since late July, and diesel in America has never cost more - 5 dollars 85 a gallon. The seven biggest oil countries met on Sunday and agreed to keep pumping exactly the same amount next month instead of more. Think of it like a shop with high prices refusing to restock: either the shelves in the back are emptier than they say, or they are keeping the last of it for an emergency. Either way, it means high prices have room to go higher.
brief: Iran said it hit an American boat with no crew on it, near the entrance to the Gulf. The American military said that is a total lie - and so far nobody has shown a picture of a damaged boat, which is why we are treating it as a claim and not a fact.

Two American envoys went to Ukraine after meeting Russia's leader, and everyone called the talks good. But Ukraine's president then said he expects the war to keep going all winter, and asked Europe for help if it does. That is what someone says when a deal is not close.

In one part of Germany, a far-right party got 44.5 out of every 100 votes - more than double the next party - and a record number of people turned out to vote. But it may still not get to run the state, because every other party has promised never to work with it.

The countries that produce most of the world's oil met online and decided not to pump any extra next month, even though oil is expensive. That is unusual, and it suggests they do not have much extra left to give.

Israeli air strikes in southern Lebanon killed seven people and destroyed government offices and an old hospital. Lebanon's president asked America to step in and stop it, because America helped write the peace deal that is supposed to prevent exactly this.

risk.line: HIGH, unchanged, and the honest read of this pass is that the loudest item is the least verifiable. Iran said it struck an unmanned US vessel entering the Strait of Hormuz; the US military called the claim a total lie; and no hull, tow or insurer entry exists on either side of that sentence. That is the shape of the whole day in the Gulf - a day after CENTCOM hit three Iranian tankers off Kharg Island, near Jask and in the Gulf of Oman in reply to ballistic missiles that a carrier and a destroyer both evaded, there is still no struck US-flagged hull and no confirmed American death, which are the two written conditions for CRITICAL. Underneath the exchange, the cartel told you more than the belligerents did: OPEC+ held October output at September's 31.01 million barrels a day, breaking four straight monthly increases, with Brent near $96 and US diesel at a record $5.85. A group that will not sell more into that price is a group preserving the last spare capacity in the world, and that is a supply-side risk the board should carry even on a quiet day. The two political items to keep in view are Saxony-Anhalt, where the AfD took 44.5 per cent on record 80 per cent turnout and still may not govern, and Kyiv, where two US envoys left with the word substantive and Zelensky budgeted out loud for a winter of war.

forecasts.q: Major US/Israeli strike campaign on Iran resumes
forecasts.note: ANCHOR RAISED 30 to 38 and RESOLUTION CRITERIA PINNED; the mark HELD at 49. The old anchor was a recurrence hazard set during a month with no US-Iran kinetic exchange, and the reference class after a confirmed exchange of fire between the two states' forces is a different and higher one - logged with its reason, because raising an anchor to shrink a divergence is exactly the move an auditor should distrust, which is why the forecast itself was not moved on it. The more important item is the criteria pin. This question is at 49 and rising into a week of US-confirmed strikes on three Iranian tankers, an IRGC ballistic-missile attack on US warships, Iranian fire into Kuwaiti and Emirati air bases, and a US bombardment of southern Iran. The daily notes had been treating the wording as an informal cap on raises, which is not a resolution rule - and NITC tankers are state-owned, so an interested reading could score this YES today. Pinned now, stricter, while the ambiguity is against our own interest: YES requires strikes on two or more distinct calendar days against targets on Iranian sovereign territory - military installations, IRGC facilities, nuclear sites or onshore energy infrastructure. Vessels at sea do not count, state-owned or not, and neither do strikes on proxies or on third-country hosts. Held rather than cut because the wording was already being enforced as a cap, and re-pricing one argument twice is the error this book refuses.

forecasts.q: Hormuz transits recover past 50% of pre-war volume
forecasts.note: CUT 2, and this is the move yesterday's deliberate HOLD was waiting for. Yesterday three transit-negative facts were refused because they were TEMPO facts and this question resolves on VOLUME. Today there is a volume print: Kpler counts 5-11 vessels a day with a 10-day average of 13, against roughly 130 pre-war - about 10 per cent of baseline with 80 days to the deadline - while the US Treasury Secretary asserts 17 million barrels a day. The gap between the official number and the tracked number is itself the finding and is logged as two-sided rather than quietly resolved in favour of the trackers. Independently, OPEC+ held October output unchanged with members citing Hormuz disruption as limiting the group's influence over price and share: the world's marginal-barrel authority publicly conceding it cannot arbitrate this market is the opposite of a normalising strait. Base rate doing the work: Suez took about a year to clear AFTER an agreement, and there is no agreement.

forecasts.q: Brent stays inside the $80-100 band
forecasts.note: ANCHOR CORRECTED, mark HELD at 29 - and the correction is the audit's headline finding. The scholarly anchor shown on this bar read 63 until today. That number was computed on 30 August from Brent at 88.29, 24 days to run and 35 per cent volatility, and it was never recomputed while Brent rallied 8 dollars, so this product has been publishing a 34-point divergence that was pure artefact. Recomputed today on a continuity-corrected double-barrier first passage from 96.28 with about 13 trading sessions left, survival is 46 per cent at 35 per cent vol, 36 per cent at 45 per cent vol and 26 per cent at 55 per cent vol - and Brent's own realised move, plus 9.0 per cent in five sessions, annualises near 64 per cent. The anchor is therefore 36. The mark stays at 29, modestly below the central case, on the OPEC+ drift term: October output held unchanged after six consecutive increases, the 1.65M b/d unwind paused, and most OPEC+ spare capacity physically sits behind the contested strait. Restated for the sixth session because it decides the score: this resolves on DAILY CLOSES, and the 99.38 of 2 September was intraday. First Brier due 24 September.

forecasts.q: US diesel crack spread settles back below $45/bbl before 15 Dec 2026
forecasts.note: CUT 3 because both mechanisms that could collapse a ~$101 crack toward $45 weakened on the same day. A crack falls when crude falls or when conversion capacity returns. OPEC+ declined to add October barrels, and US retail diesel printed a record $5.85 a gallon on Friday - demand meeting a binding CONVERSION constraint rather than a crude constraint. Framework: refining capital stock responds in years and crude valves in weeks, and the valves just stayed shut. Held above 25 because the Russian export ban still carries a published 30 September expiry, the only one of the three pulls that has a date on it.

forecasts.q: Yen carry stress: USD/JPY appreciates 8%+ (160 to 147.2 or below) in any 30-day window
forecasts.note: WEEKLY AUDIT CUT 26 to 24 - the plumbing NON-EVENT cut, and it is scored from the log file rather than from memory. Since daily logging began on 3 September the red board has printed RED once, on 3 September, and YELLOW on the three days since; crisis channels A to D tripped on none of them. Stablecoin float 310.6bn dollars with the weakest top-three peg at 0.9997, small-bank deposits plus 0.21 per cent over four weeks, SOFR minus EFFR at 3bp against a 10bp trigger, and the periphery channel checked against the daily scan and recorded quiet on evidence rather than by default. The house rule says a red board that produces no crisis is evidence AGAINST the crisis-routing read, not 'not yet'. This is the question that leans most directly on the long end breaking something, because a yen-carry unwind is the transmission channel from a JGB 10-year at 3 per cent into a global risk break, so it is the one that pays. The distillate question was deliberately NOT also cut: one fact may not be spent on two questions. The cut is small because one logged RED day is thin evidence, and saying so is part of the score.

forecasts.q: NEW - The FOMC raises the fed funds target range at or before the 9-10 December 2026 meeting
forecasts.note: WEEKLY AUDIT CUT 70 to 63 - too hot on a question that was one day old. It opened yesterday 20 points above its own published anchor of 50, on a qualitative regularity (dissent clustering) that the opening note itself declined to quantify. Declining to invent a figure is honest, but it is not a reason to sit 20 points above the anchor, and the 30 August rule says anything more than 10 points off must move toward it or carry a named reason. Two counter-anchors were named in the opening and then not priced: Blinder and Bernanke on looking through supply shocks - and a 4.1 per cent six-month PCE run-rate driven by 96 dollar Brent and record diesel is a supply shock - and the Fed's institutional reluctance to reverse direction within months of a cutting cycle. It stays well above the anchor at 63 because three July dissents FOR a hike is a real minority signal and three meetings remain inside the window. Kill criterion unchanged and published: holds at both 16 September and 4-5 November with the dissent bloc shrinking sends this to 45.

forecasts.q: Russia-Ukraine ceasefire holds 30+ days
forecasts.note: HELD at 20 on a confirming day, and this is the most deliberate non-move of the session. This question is the book's flagged repeat offender - moved four sessions running - and today the envoys arrived exactly as expected. An expected event confirming is worth very little. The genuinely new facts are two-sided and roughly cancel. FOR: national security advisers from Britain, France and Germany sat in some sessions, which begins to address the guarantor leg Fortna finds durable ceasefires need. AGAINST: the White House now says next steps will be announced 'in the coming weeks', a slip from days; Ushakov called three hours with Putin 'highly useful' and produced nothing; and overnight Russia launched 108 drones and missiles while Ukraine launched 258, so the pause covers CAPITALS and not the war. The dated falsifier stands: lapse on 8 September with no extension and no jointly acknowledged text sends this to 17.

forecasts.q: An AfD politician is sworn in as Minister-President of a German Land

The polls - AfD 40-41.7 per cent against CDU 22.5, Linke around 12, SPD around 8 - are the same polls the question was opened on yesterday, and re-marking on the same evidence one day later is double-counting. The arithmetic that decides tonight: a Brandmauer is a coalition instrument and is irrelevant against a majority of SEATS, which around 41 per cent can produce if enough small parties waste ballots below the five per cent threshold. Watch FDP and BSW. The base rate remains absolute and remains the anchor - no far-right party has led a German Land in 77 years.

forecasts.q: Fed's standing T-bill purchase program still running at end-2026
forecasts.note: ANCHOR RAISED 85 to 88 on a named framework; the mark HELD at 93 for the seventh session. Duffie's structural floor enters the book explicitly rather than being absorbed silently: atomic settlement raises, not lowers, the demand for central-bank money, and the payment system puts a floor under the balance sheet. That is genuine support for a bill programme that does not sunset, and it is independent of the ON RRP buffer-exhaustion argument the daily notes have been running - ON RRP at 0.68bn dollars, down 52.8 per cent on the month, with no buffer left to absorb an exit. The temptation was to spend Duffie as plus 2 on the mark. He was booked into the ANCHOR instead, because a structural argument revises the reference class while a discretionary bump on a number already at 93 is how a 93 becomes an unfalsifiable 99. Live cross-current still logged: a Fed priced to hike is not obviously a Fed that sunsets a reserve-management programme, because a policy rate does nothing about reserve adequacy.

forecasts.q: US commits to fixed Venezuelan heavy-crude export infrastructure
forecasts.note: WEEKLY AUDIT CUT 36 to 30, back to the published outside-view anchor, and this is the week's cleanest self-inflicted error - it was not a news error. This number walked 30 to 36 to 39 on 1 and 2 September and every point of that walk was bought by evidence about EQUITY AND ACCESS: the Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital taking a 35 per cent stake in the Venezuelan venture, 100-year rights over 17 fields, a 100bn dollar operator commitment, Chevron booking 7bn dollars against Carabobo. This question does not resolve on who owns the barrels. It resolves on FIXED EXPORT INFRASTRUCTURE - a dredged channel or a built terminal - and the 30 August audit pinned it to the stricter reading, funded and awarded rather than a statement of intent, under which a 100bn dollar operator commitment is exactly a statement of intent. Our own 4 September note already wrote the correct sentence, that the deal is organised around equity and access rather than around dredged channels, and then priced it as a 3-point trim. The honest consequence of that sentence is to remove the points the wrong-variable evidence bought, not to shade the total. Nothing has been dredged or built at any point since 29 August. Kill condition unchanged: 15 or below if no fixed-infrastructure commitment by February and flows stay token.

forecasts.q: US Hormuz concession within 30 days after the Xi summit
forecasts.note: HELD.
